Ming: Heads up — after the kernel-hint swap yesterday we're seeing a 12–18% tail latency regression on Mixtral-8x for some traffic patterns. Initial suspicion: paged KV fragmentation interacting poorly with RoPE scaling and a kernel mis-selection when num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads. Anyone micro-benching?

Anya: Running a quick perf trace now, will paste the hotspots.

Anya: perf top dump (short):
```
samples  pcnt  symbol
1200     32.1  kv_lookup_paged
600      16.0  kv_slot_coalesce
420      11.2  attention_kernel_fused
300       8.0  rope_scale_mul
```
Looks like the KV lookup + coalesce path is much hotter when page fragmentation > 40%.

Dave: Noted. The hint change forces the batched-fused kernel for seq>=512. That path assumes per-head KV layout (GQA-style). For MQA layouts (num_kv_heads < num_attention_heads) the kernel ends up doing extra index math and cross-head copies — explains the kv_slot_coalesce spike.

bench-bot: auto-bench: mixtral-8x seq=1024 batch=4 gqa=16 mqa=4 -> throughput -14%, p99 + 11%.

Ming: OK. Two axes to try: 1) change kernel selection heuristic to prefer the non-fused path when kv_head_ratio != 1.0, 2) experiment with interleaved vs per-head KV layouts to reduce fragmentation. Any micro numbers for interleaved?

Anya: Quick microbench comparing KV layouts (seq=1024, batch=1, gqa=16,mqa=4):
```
config: per_head_kv
throughput: 38.2 tokens/s
p99: 123ms

config: interleaved_kv
throughput: 44.9 tokens/s
p99: 105ms
```
Interleaved reduces cache miss chatter; fragmentation still occurs but coalesce costs drop ~30%.

Dave: That matches my local. Also note RoPE scaling multiplier we added increases memory touches in rope_scale_mul for long contexts — combined with fragmentation it amplifies tail. Two-pronged patch:
- kernel selector: if (seq>=512 && kv_head_ratio==1.0) -> fused; else -> fallback to scalar/batched kernel
- kv allocator: prefer interleaved page packing when mqa_ratio<1.0 and expected_context_length>768

Ming: Can we gate the selector behind a perf flag so we can A/B? Need to collect both cost and quality (numerical parity).

Dave: Yep. I'll draft PR with a feature flag: runtime.kernel_policy=auto|always_fused|safe_fallback. Default=auto (current heuristics), canary set to safe_fallback for the next 24h window.

infra-bot: canary deploy queued: canary/eng-runtime/kernel-policy=safe_fallback -> scheduled in 15m.

Anya: I'll run long-run eval overnight with production-like mixes (50/30/20 prompt length split). Will post aggregated perf + mem traces tomorrow.

Ming: If we see parity regressions from interleaved packing (rare but possible for some peeking logic), we should implement a migration shim that keeps old layout for pinned model versions.

Dave: Agreed. Also adding a lightweight profiler hook to emit kv_fragmentation_pct per request so we can build a routing rule (route highly-fragmented requests to dedicated pools or fallback model variants).

bench-bot: note: scheduling nightly sweep for mixtral/qwen variants with new kernel_policy.

Anya: TL;DR — probable root cause: kernel mis-selection + paged KV fragmentation worsened by RoPE scaling for long contexts. Short-term mitigation: safe_fallback kernel + interleaved KV packing for MQA cases. Longer-term: routing + allocator improvements. :thumbsup:

Ming: Thanks — keeping this thread as the coordination point. If anyone finds a quick patch that recovers p99, drop it here.

Dave: I'll open the PR and mention this thread.

Anya: I'll drop raw perf traces in this thread when the overnight run completes.

Ming: ack. :eyes:
